note: Measured failures to meet a required neutralization outcome. An entry is a DEFECT, not a waiver: the suite pins the recorded measurement, so a component that regresses further fails and a component that is fixed fails until its entry is deleted and the ceiling lowered. Nothing here is excused; everything here is owed. `publicBehaviourChange: true` marks the entries whose fix is breaking and therefore belongs to the release lane, not to a security packet. The list is EMPTY as of TASK-R2-O4 and the ceiling is 0 — which is the state this file is designed to make expensive to leave: a new entry raises a ratchet that only moves down, and the suite then asserts the recorded value in both directions.

recordedAt.admissibility: locally qualified, worktree-dirty — not release evidence

history.what: All nine `url-scheme` corpus fixtures reached the rendered `href` verbatim on all six navigation-sink components (DzButton, DzAnchor, DzBreadcrumb, DzMenu, DzSidebar, DzMegaMenu): 54 (component, sink, fixture) triples, 42 high and 12 low, every one `publicBehaviourChange: true`. Cause: no URL policy existed anywhere in packages/core/src — no scheme check, no allowlist, no normalization. Reported rather than fixed because refusing `javascript:void(0)` is a breaking change, and routed to the release lane.
history.how: One allowlist policy in the provider/contracts layer (`DZ_URL_POLICY_KEY`, `packages/core/src/security/url-policy.ts`), applied at every navigation sink including the three compound sub-parts and DzMegaMenu's four binding sites. A refused URL is OMITTED and the element renders as a non-link carrying `data-state="url-rejected"`. The corpus fixtures that measured the 54 are now the regression suite: `url-boundary.url-policy.spec.ts` and `url-boundary.malicious-corpus.spec.ts` assert `rejected` directly, with no entry here to fall back on.
